tips.title: Starting daily folic acid supplementation at 0.4 mg before pregnancy and continuing through the first trimester
tips.cost: A bottle costs only a few hundred rupees. Rural women receive it for free through the national folic acid supplementation program. The real challenge is remembering to take one pill every day.
tips.inPlainWords: Taking one folic acid pill daily before and during early pregnancy can cut the risk of neural tube defects in babies by roughly 70%. These defects include conditions like anencephaly and spina bifida. For women who’ve already had a child with such a defect, this regimen reduces the likelihood of a repeat occurrence to about one third of the original risk.
tips.benefit: A Cochrane systematic review pooled data from 5 trials involving 6,708 deliveries, rating the evidence as high quality. Daily folic acid intake before and during pregnancy lowered the relative risk of fetal neural tube defects to 0.31 (95% CI 0.17–0.58), a reduction of roughly 70%. For women with a prior child affected by neural tube defects, the relative risk dropped to 0.34 (95% CI 0.18–0.64), equating to a one third reduction in risk. No difference in effectiveness was observed between 0.4 mg and higher doses, nor between folic acid alone and multivitamin supplements.
tips.sources: De-Regil LM, Peña-Rosas JP, Fernández-Gaxiola AC, Rayco-Solon P (2015). Effects and safety of periconceptional oral folate supplementation for preventing birth defects. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (12), CD007950. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007950.pub3>
tips.caveats: The key point is to start taking folic acid *before* pregnancy. A fetus’s neural tube closes within 28 days of conception; by the time a pregnancy is detected, most of this window has already passed. Therefore, if you’re planning to conceive, begin supplementation three months in advance. The same review found no clear evidence that folic acid prevents cleft lip and palate, congenital heart disease, or miscarriage — so don’t expect it to address these issues.

tips.title: Register for the Maternal and Child Health Handbook at a community health center before 13 weeks of pregnancy to claim free prenatal checkups
tips.cost: No cost at all — this is part of the national basic public health service program. You’ll need to make several visits based on your gestational age.
tips.inPlainWords: You are entitled to at least five free prenatal checkups during pregnancy, plus home visits after delivery and a 42-day postpartum checkup, all paid for by the state. To access these services, you must register for the Maternal and Child Health Handbook at a community health center before 13 weeks of gestation. Failing to do so means you lose out on all these free services.
tips.benefit: The third edition of the National Basic Public Health Service Standards outlines specific maternal health management services available to all permanent residents who are pregnant. These include one health checkup in early pregnancy, two in mid-pregnancy, two in late pregnancy, one postpartum home visit, and one 42-day postpartum checkup. Registration for the handbook must be completed before 13 weeks of pregnancy, at which point your first prenatal checkup will also be scheduled. The two mid-pregnancy checkups occur between 16–20 weeks and 21–24 weeks respectively, while the two late-pregnancy checkups are scheduled for 28–36 weeks and 37–40 weeks. Local service lists also include a full set of initial lab tests and postpartum depression screening as part of these free services.
tips.sources: Jingjiang Municipal People's Government. National Basic Public Health Service Project - Maternal Health Management Service (Local service list is public). <https://www.jingjiang.gov.cn/xxgk/zdlyxxgk/wsjk/art/2023/art_383017a2e7794892bc772bfbe042f379.html>
tips.caveats: These five free checkups represent the minimum number of services provided; they do not cover all possible prenatal tests. Depending on your individual health needs, your doctor may recommend additional ultrasounds, blood glucose tests, or fetal heart rate monitoring, all of which will incur extra costs. Registering for the handbook as early as possible also allows for earlier assessment of your pregnancy risk level. This risk grading system categorizes pregnant women based on their individual risk factors, ensuring those identified as high-risk receive timely care at specialized medical facilities. Even if you live in a different district than your registered household location, you can still register at your current place of residence — there is no requirement to return to your place of household registration.

tips.title: Getting tested for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B during the first prenatal visit — free prevention options available
tips.cost: No cost involved; the maternal and infant transmission prevention program provides these tests at no charge.
tips.inPlainWords: During your very first prenatal checkup, you can get tested for HIV, syphilis, and hepatitis B at no personal expense. Even if results show a positive diagnosis, there are still effective ways to prevent transmission to your baby. The government offers free medication and treatment plans to block the spread of these infections from mother to child — this is known as maternal and infant transmission prevention.
tips.benefit: Maternal and infant transmission is how infections pass from a mother to her unborn or newborn child. The “Work Specifications for Preventing Maternal and Infant Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B (2020 Edition)” mandates that during early pregnancy or at the first prenatal visit, healthcare providers must share relevant information and “offer appropriate, standardized free testing” — meaning these three tests are completely free. Follow-up counseling and referrals are also provided based on test results. A positive diagnosis is not a dead end: Article 44 of the “Regulations on HIV/AIDS Prevention and Control” guarantees free treatment and counseling for pregnant women living with HIV to prevent transmission to their babies. Article 43 further requires that such women receive services including transmission prevention, treatment, postpartum home visits, infant follow-ups, and testing. For mothers who test positive for hepatitis B surface antigen, newborns receive both hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth (see Section 20, Item 2).
tips.sources: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; National Health Authority. <https://nha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Early testing is especially valuable for these three conditions, as both prevention and treatment require sufficient time to be effective. Article 3 of the “Regulations on HIV/AIDS Prevention and Control” also states that “no entity or individual may discriminate against people living with HIV/AIDS, AIDS patients, or their family members”; their legal rights related to marriage, employment, medical care, and education are fully protected by law. General prevention measures and routine testing are covered in Section 1, while post-exposure prophylaxis after high-risk behaviors is detailed in Section 13.

tips.title: No smoking or drinking at all throughout pregnancy — and no one else in the house should smoke either
tips.cost: There’s no cost at all; in fact, it saves money on cigarettes and alcohol. The real challenge is getting everyone living in the same house to quit alongside the pregnant woman.
tips.inPlainWords: Smoking during pregnancy raises the chances of premature birth, a baby being born underweight, and cleft lip or palate. It also doubles the risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and childbirth, and increases the risk of sudden infant death syndrome. Secondhand smoke from anyone smoking indoors counts just the same. It is never too late to quit, no matter when you start.
tips.benefit: According to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, smoking during pregnancy can result in babies being “born at full term but still underweight” and “more likely to be born prematurely.” It “doubles the risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and childbirth,” raises the risk of birth defects such as cleft lip and palate, and “damages the developing lungs and brain of the fetus, with effects lasting into childhood.” Babies born to mothers who smoke during pregnancy, as well as infants exposed to smoke after birth, face a higher risk of sudden infant death syndrome. Official guidance states that “it is best to quit smoking before getting pregnant, but quitting while already pregnant still provides benefits,” and “it is never too late to quit.”
tips.sources: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Smoking During Pregnancy. <https://www.cdc.gov/tobacco/campaign/tips/diseases/pregnancy.html>
tips.caveats: Secondhand smoke from anyone smoking indoors is just as harmful to the fetus as direct smoking. Therefore, this rule applies to the whole household, not just the pregnant woman. The same principle holds true for alcohol: there is no known safe level of alcohol consumption during pregnancy, so the safest approach is to avoid it entirely. The impact of smoking and drinking on the health of adults themselves is covered in Section 2.

tips.title: For women at high risk of preeclampsia, start taking one low-dose aspirin tablet daily after week 12 of pregnancy
tips.cost: a few hundred rupees. One tablet per day must be taken until delivery. The hard part is remembering to take it every single day.
tips.inPlainWords: Preeclampsia is a type of high blood pressure that occurs during pregnancy. Women falling into any of these six categories are at high risk: those who had preeclampsia in a previous pregnancy, women carrying multiples, women with chronic hypertension, women with diabetes prior to pregnancy, women with kidney disease, and women with autoimmune diseases. For these women, taking one low-dose aspirin tablet daily starting at week 12 can reduce the risk of preeclampsia by roughly 15%, the risk of premature birth by about 20%, and the risk of perinatal death by nearly 20%. Women not in these categories should not take it on their own.
tips.benefit: The US Preventive Services Task Force gives this a Grade B recommendation: for women at high risk of preeclampsia, taking low-dose aspirin (81 mg per day) after week 12 of pregnancy can help prevent the condition. Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder unique to pregnancy. Results from multiple studies combined show the following outcomes, with 95% confidence intervals provided as ranges of reliability. The relative risk of preeclampsia drops to 0.85 (95% CI: 0.75 to 0.95, based on 16 studies), a reduction of roughly 15%. The relative risk of premature birth is 0.80 (95% CI: 0.67 to 0.95, based on 13 studies), a drop of about 20%. The relative risk of perinatal death — death occurring around the time of childbirth — is 0.79 (95% CI: 0.66 to 0.96, based on 11 studies), a reduction of roughly 21%. The relative risk of small-for-gestational-age infants or intrauterine growth restriction is 0.82 (95% CI: 0.68 to 0.99, based on 16 studies), a decrease of around 18%, meaning fetuses are less likely to be smaller than expected for their gestational age.
tips.sources: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication. <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/low-dose-aspirin-use-for-the-prevention-of-morbidity-and-mortality-from-preeclampsia-preventive-medication>
tips.caveats: The groups considered high risk include women who had preeclampsia in a prior pregnancy, those carrying twins or multiples, women with chronic hypertension, women with type 1 or type 2 diabetes prior to pregnancy, women with kidney disease, and women with autoimmune diseases such as systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome. Women not in these groups should not take aspirin on their own. This medication requires a doctor’s prescription; be sure to share your full medical history during prenatal checkups so your doctor can make an appropriate assessment.

tips.title: Get screened for gestational diabetes at 24 weeks of gestation or later — don’t mind drinking the sugary solution
tips.cost: Several tens to over a hundred rupees. You must fast beforehand, and several blood draws will take up half a morning.
tips.inPlainWords: Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that appears only during pregnancy. At 24 weeks or later, spending half a morning drinking a sugary solution and having several blood tests can detect it. Skipping this test raises the risks of having a macrosomic baby, difficult labor, cesarean delivery, preeclampsia, and neonatal hypoglycemia.
tips.benefit: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force recommends screening for gestational diabetes at 24 weeks or later for asymptomatic pregnant women — those who feel no symptoms at all. Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that appears only during pregnancy. This single screening test should be done at 24 weeks or later. The Task Force concluded that current evidence does not show any clear benefits or harms from screening before 24 weeks (Grade I). Untreated gestational diabetes increases the risks of macrosomia, difficult labor, cesarean delivery, preeclampsia, and neonatal hypoglycemia.
tips.sources: US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Gestational Diabetes: Screening. <https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recommendation/gestational-diabetes-screening>
tips.caveats: Most women diagnosed with gestational diabetes can control their blood sugar through diet and exercise alone; only a minority need insulin injections. Don’t skip this test out of fear of being told you need insulin. After giving birth, you must get another blood sugar test — women who’ve had gestational diabetes face a significantly higher risk of developing type 2 diabetes later on.

tips.title: Memorize this “go to the hospital immediately” checklist — it applies throughout pregnancy and the first year after childbirth
tips.cost: No cost at all. It takes just five minutes to memorize, and it’s a good idea to share it with anyone living in the same household.
tips.inPlainWords: If any of the following symptoms appear, head to the hospital on the same day — do not wait until the next morning. Persistent or worsening headaches, changes in vision, fever reaching 38°C. Severe swelling of the hands or face, trouble breathing, chest pain or a rapid heartbeat. Unrelenting severe abdominal pain, no fetal movement or a noticeable drop in fetal movement. Vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage. Swelling, pain and redness in one arm or leg. Thoughts of harming yourself or your baby. The full list is included in the Benefits section below. These guidelines apply equally in the first year after childbirth.
tips.benefit: These are all emergency warning signs during pregnancy and postpartum listed by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Persistent or worsening headaches, dizziness or fainting, changes in vision, a body temperature of 38°C or higher. Severe swelling of the hands or face, thoughts of harming yourself or your baby. Difficulty breathing, chest pain or a rapid heartbeat. Severe nausea and vomiting, unrelenting severe abdominal pain. Absence or significant reduction of fetal movement during pregnancy, vaginal bleeding or fluid leakage during pregnancy or postpartum. Abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge after childbirth. Severe swelling, redness and pain in one arm or leg. None of these issues disappear after the postpartum recovery period — they can all occur within the first year after childbirth.
tips.sources: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Hear Her — Urgent Maternal Warning Signs. <https://www.cdc.gov/hearher/maternal-warning-signs/index.html>; World Health Organization. Maternal mortality fact sheet. <https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/maternal-mortality>
tips.caveats: This checklist serves to clearly distinguish between situations where you can wait a little longer and those that demand immediate medical attention. Headaches paired with blurred vision and upper abdominal pain are typical signs of preeclampsia, a form of pregnancy-related hypertension. Swelling and pain in one lower leg often indicates deep vein thrombosis (see Section 13). According to the World Health Organization, severe postpartum hemorrhage can be fatal to a healthy woman within just a few hours. If any of these symptoms appear, go to the hospital right away — do not delay by waiting at home overnight.

tips.title: If your water breaks, lie down flat, elevate your hips, and call 112 — don’t walk around or take a shower
tips.cost: No cost at all
tips.inPlainWords: If your water breaks, there’s no time to calmly gather your things and head out. The right thing to do is lie down right where you are, raise your hips, and call 112 immediately. Walking around while standing up causes amniotic fluid to leak even faster, and the umbilical cord can be pulled out along with it. This is a life-threatening emergency for the baby.
tips.benefit: This is exactly what the Beijing Municipal Health Commission recommends: “Immediately lie down flat to prevent further loss of amniotic fluid,” “Do not walk around casually,” and “Call emergency services at 120 right away.” While waiting for help, inform family members so they can bring necessary items to the hospital. Medical sources further explain why this is essential: when a person stands, amniotic fluid drains much more quickly, increasing the risk of umbilical cord prolapse — a critical emergency for the fetus. Therefore, lying down and elevating the hips is crucial; a left-side lying position is ideal.
tips.sources: Beijing Municipal Health Commission. Weekly first aid topic: What should expectant mothers do if their amniotic fluid breaks prematurely? <https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/bmfw_20143/jkzs/jzjj/202001/t20200115_1575632.html>; Beijing Shunyi District Maternal and Child Health Hospital. What should I do if my water breaks at home in late pregnancy? <https://www.bch-syfy.cn/Html/News/Articles/9453.html>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>; National Health Authority. <https://nha.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The three main signs of impending labor are regular contractions, vaginal bleeding, and water breaking. With the first two, you can still prepare calmly, but water breaking demands immediate action: lie down and call for help. Common mistakes include showering, squatting on the toilet, or driving yourself to the hospital. Be sure to note the exact time water broke and its color; tell the doctor if it appears yellow-green or contains meconium, as this indicates fetal distress and oxygen deprivation. If you also experience regular contractions, a marked drop in fetal movement, fever, or chills, emphasize that this is a true emergency.

tips.title: Ask for labor analgesia — it does not raise the risk of C-section
tips.cost: Several hundred to over ₹14,200; prices vary by region. Be sure to ask the hospital and anesthesiology department in advance whether this service is available. The main hurdle is simply bringing it up yourself.
tips.inPlainWords: Labor analgesia involves injecting anesthetic into the lower back to dull the pain of childbirth. It works far better than other pain‑relief options and does not make a C-section more likely. The claim that “it causes lifelong back pain” is also unfounded. Nowadays it is offered as a separate charge, so hospitals are more willing to provide it.
tips.benefit: A Cochrane systematic review found that epidural analgesia is more effective than non‑epidural methods at reducing labor pain and improving maternal satisfaction. Labor analgesia uses exactly this technique. The same review states that epidural analgesia has no effect on the risk of C-section or long‑term back pain. Instrumental delivery — using tools to assist birth — shows no increased incidence in studies published after 2005. Starting in 2024, the National Healthcare Security Administration introduced separate pricing categories for “labor analgesia,” “doula‑assisted childbirth,” and “family‑member labor support,” precisely because previously there were no dedicated rates to motivate hospitals to offer these services.
tips.sources: Anim-Somuah M, Smyth RMD, Cyna AM, Cuthbert A (2018). Epidural versus non-epidural or no analgesia for pain management in labor. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (5), CD000331. <https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000331.pub4>; National Medical Security Administration (2024). Reconstructing obstetric service price projects to help build a childbirth-friendly society. <https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202406/content_6957553.htm>
tips.caveats: Both popular myths — “epidural analgesia causes lifelong back pain” and “it makes a C-section more likely” — lack any scientific basis. Cochrane’s comparison of epidural analgesia with other pain‑relief methods confirms it has no impact on C‑section risk or chronic back problems. Real side effects may include low blood pressure, fever, weak legs, difficulty urinating, longer first‑ and second‑stage labor, and a higher need for oxytocin. The decision to use it is yours; don’t let unfounded rumors deter you. Availability also depends on whether the hospital has an anesthesiologist on duty 24/7 — be sure to ask during prenatal visits.

tips.title: Don’t request a C-section without medical indication, and avoid scheduling one just to pick a “lucky” date
tips.cost: No direct cost. The real challenge is resisting pressure from family members.
tips.inPlainWords: According to the World Health Organization, once the C-section rate in a region exceeds 10%, further reductions in maternal and neonatal mortality become unlikely. When a C-section is medically necessary, it must be performed. However, opting for one solely to choose a favorable date or to avoid labor pain means undergoing a major abdominal operation for no real reason.
tips.benefit: A 2015 WHO statement notes that when C-section rates rise to roughly 10% in a population, maternal and neonatal deaths decline. Beyond that threshold, there is no evidence of additional mortality benefits. WHO also stresses that every effort should be made to provide C-sections to women who truly need them, rather than aiming for a specific percentage target.
tips.sources: World Health Organization (2015). WHO Statement on Caesarean Section Rates (WHO/RHR/15.02). <https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-RHR-15.02>
tips.caveats: This guidance does not oppose C-sections. When medically warranted, they are life-saving procedures and should be performed without hesitation. What it discourages is undergoing a C-section when there is no medical need—such as to avoid labor pain, to pick an auspicious date, or to influence a child’s future age for school enrollment. The trade-offs are significant: C-sections are major abdominal surgeries with slower recovery times, and they increase risks of placenta previa, placenta accreta, and uterine rupture in subsequent pregnancies—factors that may affect a woman’s decision to have more children.

tips.title: Check your maternity cover before pregnancy: ESIC, PM-JAY or a state scheme may pay for the delivery
tips.cost: ESIC and PM-JAY are contribution or eligibility based; a public facility is free. A private policy's premium and waiting period apply.
tips.inPlainWords: India has no single maternity insurance for everyone. An insured worker under ESIC gets maternity benefit and medical care; an eligible household under PM-JAY gets hospital cover; some states run a maternity scheme. A private policy may have a waiting period. Check the cover, the empanelled hospital and the documents before you conceive, not during labour.
tips.benefit: The ESIC maternity benefit includes a cash benefit for the insured woman and medical treatment. PM-JAY covers maternity and newborn care for eligible households at empanelled hospitals. The Pradhan Mantri Matru Vandana Yojana gives a cash benefit to an eligible woman for the first living child. A private health policy may cover maternity after a waiting period. The National Health Mission runs free delivery services at public facilities.
tips.sources: Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>; National Health Authority, PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/>; Ministry of Women and Child Development, PMMVY. <https://wcd.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A policy bought after conception may exclude the pregnancy. A cashless claim needs pre-authorisation. Keep the antenatal records and the scheme card.

tips.title: Get the birth registered and the certificate early; the hospital gives the birth report and the registrar issues the certificate
tips.cost: The registration fee is small; a late fee applies after 21 days.
tips.inPlainWords: The hospital reports the birth to the local registrar under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, and the family can apply for the birth certificate. Register within 21 days to avoid a late fee. Decide the baby's name before the registration if the state requires it. The birth certificate is needed for the Aadhaar, the school admission and the passport.
tips.benefit: The 1969 Act requires the birth to be registered within 21 days; a late registration needs the registrar's permission and a fee. The hospital issues a birth report, and the municipal registrar issues the certificate. A name can be added later in some states. The certificate is the basis for the Aadhaar enrolment and the school record.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs, civil registration. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Unique Identification Authority of India. <https://uidai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: Check the spelling of the name and the parents' details before you leave the registrar. A correction needs an affidavit and a fee. Do not pay an agent to 'fast-track' a birth certificate.

tips.title: Don’t skip newborn heel‑prick and hearing tests
tips.cost: In most areas these tests are free; otherwise they cost only a few hundred rupees. Some extra screening items may require out‑of‑pocket payment.
tips.inPlainWords: A single heel‑prick blood test and one hearing test can detect hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, and hearing loss even when the baby appears perfectly healthy. By the time symptoms become obvious, any intellectual damage is already irreversible.
tips.benefit: Article 3 of the “Administrative Measures for Newborn Disease Screening” lists congenital hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, other inherited metabolic disorders, and hearing impairment as nationally mandated screening targets. All of these conditions show no outward signs early on; once symptoms appear, lasting intellectual harm has already occurred. Early detection and prompt treatment—such as thyroid hormone replacement, special formula milk, hearing aids, or cochlear implants—yield excellent outcomes. Article 10 further stipulates that any positive screening result must be promptly communicated to parents for confirmatory diagnosis.
tips.sources: Ministry of Health (2009). Measures for the Management of Newborn Disease Screening (Ministry of Health Order No. 64, Articles 3, 10, and 11). <http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2009/content_1371363.htm>
tips.caveats: Article 11 requires that before screening, parents be fully informed of the tests, eligibility criteria, procedures, sensitivity rates, and associated costs, and must give written consent. Consequently, you’ll receive an informed‑consent form. Carefully review which conditions are covered by the state program and which extra items incur personal fees. A positive initial result does not mean a definitive diagnosis; most infants are cleared after a single follow‑up test, so there’s no need to panic at this stage. If a newborn fails the initial hearing screen, follow the instructions for a repeat test—don’t assume “if the baby seems to hear, it’s fine.”

tips.title: Add the newborn to your health cover early: PM-JAY or ESIC can cover the baby without waiting for Aadhaar
tips.cost: PM-JAY is free for an eligible household. ESIC is contribution based.
tips.inPlainWords: A newborn can be covered under PM-JAY or ESIC as a dependant, usually without an Aadhaar of their own. The mother's card and the birth certificate are enough for the initial enrolment; the Aadhaar can be added later. Do not wait for the birth registration to be complete before you ask the scheme office. A delay can leave the baby uninsured for the first weeks.
tips.benefit: PM-JAY covers the newborn as part of the eligible household, and the scheme's guidelines allow enrolment with the mother's card and the birth record. ESIC covers the insured person's dependants, including a newborn. The National Health Mission's public facilities provide newborn care. The Aadhaar is not mandatory for a newborn's emergency treatment.
tips.sources: National Health Authority, PM-JAY. <https://nha.gov.in/>; Employees' State Insurance Corporation. <https://esic.gov.in/>; Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. <https://mohfw.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: The enrolment process differs by state. A private policy may have a waiting period for a newborn. Keep the birth certificate and the mother's card.

tips.title: Register the birth with the municipal registrar within 21 days — not at a police station
tips.cost: The fee is small; a late fee applies after 21 days.
tips.inPlainWords: A birth is registered with the local municipal registrar under the Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969, not with the police. The hospital usually reports the birth; the family applies for the certificate. If the birth is at home, the family must report it to the registrar. Register within 21 days to avoid a late fee and a longer process.
tips.benefit: The 1969 Act requires registration within 21 days. The hospital's birth report and the parents' identity proof are the main documents. A late registration needs the registrar's permission and a fee. The certificate is required for the Aadhaar, the school admission and the passport. A police station has no role in a normal birth registration.
tips.sources: Registration of Births and Deaths Act, 1969. <https://www.indiacode.nic.in/>; Ministry of Home Affairs, civil registration. <https://crsorgi.gov.in/>; Unique Identification Authority of India. <https://uidai.gov.in/>
tips.caveats: A home birth needs a witness and a medical certificate where available. Check the name spelling. A correction needs an affidavit.

tips.title: Don’t skip that 42-day postpartum checkup — it also screens for postpartum depression
tips.cost: It’s free; it’s part of basic public health services. It takes half a day. The hard part is that right after childbirth you often feel too lazy to go.
tips.inPlainWords: This checkup costs nothing and includes a complete blood count, vaginal discharge test, plus a screening for postpartum depression. Serious problems can arise at any time during the first year after birth, so don’t assume you’re out of danger just because the postpartum period is over.
tips.benefit: According to the “National Standards for Basic Public Health Services (3rd Edition),” postpartum care requires one home visit and one health checkup at 42 days. Local service lists confirm this visit includes lab tests (blood count, vaginal discharge) and a postpartum depression screening. Severe complications may appear throughout the first year. Items on the “Go to the hospital immediately” list in Section 7 — such as “thoughts of harming oneself or the baby,” “abnormal vaginal bleeding or discharge,” or “severe swelling/pain in one limb” — all fall under postpartum risks.
tips.sources: Jingjiang Municipal People's Government. National Basic Public Health Service Project - Maternal Health Management Service (Local service list is public). <https://www.jingjiang.gov.cn/xxgk/zdlyxxgk/wsjk/art/2023/art_383017a2e7794892bc772bfbe042f379.html>
tips.caveats: Postpartum depression isn’t a sign of weakness or something that can be fixed by family telling you to “cheer up.” There are specific screening questionnaires and treatments available, and recovery is possible. Handling suicidal thoughts is covered in Section 1. Legal options if caring for a newborn proves impossible are outlined in Section 9, Item 20. This checkup also evaluates wound healing, uterine recovery, pelvic floor function, and discusses contraception — remember, the absence of menstruation after childbirth doesn’t mean pregnancy is impossible.

tips.title: You do not need to give away your cat during pregnancy: delegate daily litter box cleaning, cook all meat thoroughly, and wear gloves when gardening
tips.cost: Zero monetary cost. Have another household member scoop the litter box daily. If you must clean it yourself, use disposable gloves. The willpower challenge is ensuring all meat consumed is cooked thoroughly and skipping rare steaks or cured charcuterie.
tips.inPlainWords: Toxoplasmosis is caused by an intracellular parasite. Primary infection acquired during pregnancy can cause miscarriage, stillbirth, or severe congenital ocular and neurological damage in the infant. However, living with a domestic cat does not increase the risk of infection, and there is no medical reason to rehome family cats. The primary routes of transmission are consuming undercooked meat, eating unwashed produce, or touching contaminated garden soil. Simply delegate litter box duty to someone else and change it daily.
tips.benefit: According to the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) and the UK National Health Service (NHS), newly acquired maternal toxoplasmosis infection shortly before or during pregnancy can transmit vertically to the fetus. While many congenitally infected newborns appear asymptomatic at birth, untreated infants frequently develop chorioretinitis, blindness, or intellectual disability later in life, and a subset present at birth with severe hydrocephalus, microcephaly, or intracranial calcifications. In a multicenter cohort of 603 pregnant women with confirmed toxoplasma infection, mother-to-child transmission averaged 29% overall (95% CI 25%–33%), rising from 6% at 13 weeks of gestation to 72% at 36 weeks, with fetal clinical damage peaking when infection occurred between 24 and 30 weeks (approximately 10% risk of severe early clinical manifestations). In a landmark 6-center European case-control study (Cook et al., BMJ), domestic cat ownership was not associated with increased risk of acute maternal infection (OR 1.0, 95% CI 0.7–1.5), and cleaning litter boxes showed no statistically significant excess risk (OR 1.3, 95% CI 0.8–2.1). In contrast, consuming undercooked lamb or beef increased risk more than threefold (OR 3.13, 95% CI 1.4–7.2), and soil contact increased risk by 81% (OR 1.81, 95% CI 1.2–2.7). Between 30% and 63% of acute infections in European cities were attributable to undercooked or cured meat, and 6% to 17% to soil exposure. CDC and NHS clinical protocols specify that pregnant women should delegate litter cleaning to another person. If unavoidable, wear disposable gloves and wash hands thoroughly with soap. Litter boxes must be emptied daily, as Toxoplasma oocysts in feline feces require 1 to 5 days to become infectious. Pregnant women should avoid acquiring new cats or handling stray kittens, keep household cats indoors, and feed them commercial cooked or canned food rather than raw meat.

tips.caveats: Cats shed oocysts only for a brief 1- to 3-week window following their initial infection; adult indoor cats previously exposed rarely shed again. An indoor cat fed commercial pet food has virtually zero risk of contracting or shedding the parasite. Conversely, households without pets frequently contract toxoplasmosis from raw or undercooked meat, unwashed raw vegetables, contaminated garden soil, or untreated water. Essential preventative behaviors: cook whole cuts of meat and ground meats to safe internal temperatures; wash cutting boards, knives, and hands thoroughly after handling raw meat; rinse all fruits and vegetables under running water; wear gloves when gardening or handling soil, followed by handwashing. The NHS also cautions against consuming dry-cured meats (e.g., salami, Parma ham) unless cooked, and avoiding unpasteurized goat milk. Consult your obstetrician regarding toxoplasma antibody screening (TORCH panel) during prenatal care. Benefit magnitude is categorized as Moderate based on preserving family companion animals while preventing severe fetal neurological injury. Primary beneficiaries are yourself and your child.

tips.title: Receive an inactivated influenza vaccine during pregnancy if pregnant during flu season; it can be administered at any gestational stage, but avoid live-attenuated nasal sprays
tips.cost: Out of pocket, a flu vaccine costs a few tens of dollars; requires one visit to a community vaccination clinic. The only friction is selecting a brand whose product leaflet does not list pregnancy as an absolute contraindication.
tips.inPlainWords: Pregnant women face significantly higher risks of hospitalization from influenza than non-pregnant individuals. Receiving a flu shot during pregnancy reduces the mother's risk of flu-related hospitalization by roughly 40%. It also cuts laboratory-confirmed influenza in infants during their first 6 months of life by approximately half, and cuts infant flu hospitalizations by roughly 70%. Evidence shows no increase in miscarriage, stillbirth, or congenital anomalies.
tips.benefit: The World Health Organization (WHO) 2022 influenza position paper highlights that pregnant women have an odds ratio of 6.8 (95% CI 6.0–7.7) for flu-related hospitalization compared to non-pregnant peers. A randomized controlled trial in Bangladesh enrolled 340 pregnant women assigned to inactivated influenza vaccine or pneumococcal control, followed through 24 weeks postpartum: vaccine efficacy against laboratory-confirmed influenza in infants was 63% (95% CI 5%–85%), while maternal febrile respiratory illness was reduced by 36% (95% CI 4%–57%). In double-blind placebo-controlled trials in South Africa, maternal vaccination reduced confirmed influenza by 50.4% in mothers and 48.8% in infants. A meta-analysis pooling four trials and three observational cohorts demonstrated that maternal vaccination reduced infant laboratory-confirmed influenza in the first 6 months of life by 48% (95% CI 33%–59%) and infant influenza hospitalizations by 72% (95% CI 39%–87%). A multi-country retrospective study across four nations (2010–2016) demonstrated a 40% reduction (95% CI 12%–59%) in maternal laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations. In terms of safety, a systematic review of 40 studies found no excess risk of stillbirth (aOR 0.84, 95% CI 0.65–1.08) or congenital malformations (aOR 1.03, 95% CI 0.99–1.07), while preterm birth was reduced by 13% (aOR 0.87, 95% CI 0.78–0.96). A US Vaccine Safety Datalink study of three influenza seasons (2012–2015) found no association between vaccination in the preceding 28 days and spontaneous abortion (aOR 0.9, 95% CI 0.6–1.5).

tips.caveats: Controversy: A 2017 US study reported an association between first-trimester flu vaccination and spontaneous abortion within 28 days among women also vaccinated with pH1N1 in the prior season (aOR 2.0, 95% CI 1.1–3.6); however, the authors noted potential confounding, and subsequent larger investigations across three subsequent seasons failed to replicate this association. Live attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV nasal spray) is strictly contraindicated in pregnancy; only injectable inactivated influenza vaccines should be administered. Because infants younger than 6 months cannot receive flu vaccination directly, maternal vaccination constitutes their primary antibody defense against winter influenza. For adult routine flu vaccination evidence, see Chapter 1, Rule 20.

tips.title: Sleep on your side after 28 weeks of pregnancy — either left or right — and avoid sleeping flat on your back
tips.cost: Free. The only friction is consciously adapting sleep posture for individuals accustomed to sleeping supine.
tips.inPlainWords: Going to sleep on your back (supine position) after 28 weeks of gestation is associated with roughly 2.6 times the risk of late stillbirth compared to sleeping on your side. Left and right sides are equally safe; choose whichever side feels comfortable. If you wake up on your back during the night, do not panic — simply roll back onto your side before going back to sleep.
tips.benefit: An individual participant data meta-analysis pooling 5 case-control studies across New Zealand, Australia, the UK, and international registries (851 stillbirth cases and 2,257 healthy controls) evaluated maternal going-to-sleep position in late pregnancy (after 28 weeks). Compared to going to sleep on the left side, supine going-to-sleep position was associated with a 2.6-fold increase in late stillbirth risk (adjusted odds ratio aOR 2.63, 95% CI 1.72–4.04). Right-side sleep showed no elevated risk compared to left (aOR 1.04, 95% CI 0.83–1.31). The association remained consistent across maternal BMI categories and fetal growth percentiles. Authors estimated that if all pregnant women after 28 weeks avoided supine going-to-sleep positions, late stillbirths could theoretically be reduced by approximately 5.8% (95% CI 3.2%–9.2%). The UK NHS endorses side sleeping after 28 weeks as a standard risk-reduction recommendation, reassuring mothers that waking up supine is harmless as long as they turn onto their side again.
tips.sources: Cronin RS, Li M, Thompson JMD, et al. (2019). EClinicalMedicine, 10, 49-57. <https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eclinm.2019.03.014>; Silver RM, Hunter S, Reddy UM, et al. (2019). tips.caveats: Controversy: Findings rely on retrospective recall of going-to-sleep position by mothers after stillbirth occurred, introducing potential recall bias. A prospective US cohort of 8,706 nulliparous women evaluated sleep position up to 30 weeks of gestation and found no association between non-left or supine sleeping and composite adverse pregnancy outcomes (aOR 0.99, 95% CI 0.89–1.11); however, the prospective study did not capture sleep position during the third trimester beyond 30 weeks. Because side sleeping has zero cost and carries no clinical risk, major health agencies endorse side-sleeping as prudent precautionary care. High-income country late stillbirth rates range between 1.3 and 8.8 per 1,000 births.

tips.title: Use effective contraception once sexual intercourse resumes postpartum, as breastfeeding is not reliable birth control; wait at least 18 months before conceiving the next child
tips.cost: Condoms cost a few dollars per box. Subdermal implants or IUD placement require an outpatient clinic visit. The challenge is remembering to manage contraception amid the exhaustion of newborn care.
tips.inPlainWords: Ovulation can resume as early as 3 weeks postpartum, even while nursing and before menstruation returns. Lactational amenorrhea method (LAM) prevents over 99% of pregnancies only if three strict conditions are simultaneously met: exclusive breastfeeding, complete absence of menses, and infant under 6 months. If any condition lapses, another birth control method is essential. Conceiving less than 6 months after delivery increases preterm birth risk by approximately 40%; the World Health Organization recommends waiting at least 18 to 24 months before conceiving again.
tips.benefit: The UK NHS states pregnancy is possible 3 weeks after childbirth. A meta-analysis of 67 studies evaluating birth spacing found that interpregnancy intervals under 6 months (measured from prior birth to next conception) were associated with a 40% increased risk of preterm birth (OR 1.40, 95% CI 1.24–1.58), a 61% increase in low birth weight (OR 1.61, 95% CI 1.39–1.86), and a 26% increase in small-for-gestational-age infants (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.18–1.33) compared to intervals of 18–23 months. A Canadian cohort study of 148,000 pregnancies comparing 6-month vs. 18-month intervals showed that among mothers aged 35 and older, maternal severe morbidity or mortality was 0.62% vs. 0.26% (adjusted risk ratio aRR 2.39, 95% CI 2.03–2.80); for infants of mothers aged 20–34, adverse perinatal outcomes were 2.0% vs. 1.4% (aRR 1.42, 95% CI 1.36–1.47). The World Health Organization recommends a minimum interpregnancy interval of 24 months (and at least 6 months following a miscarriage or induced abortion) to allow maternal physiological and micronutrient replenishment.

tips.caveats: Controversy: Optimal intervals remain debated between 18 and 24 months, with NHS recommending at least 12 months. An Australian within-mother matched sibling cohort study suggested that part of the short-interval risk may stem from unmeasured maternal socioeconomic factors (within-mother OR 1.07 for preterm birth). However, the necessity of proactive contraception itself is uncontroversial. Barrier condoms and progestin-only implants can be initiated immediately postpartum, while combined oral contraceptives should generally wait until at least 6 weeks postpartum if breastfeeding. Discuss contraceptive selection during the routine 42-day postpartum examination (Chapter 27, Rule 16).
